references.text: Laban learns of Jacob's flight three days later, and God warns him in a dream. This shows the consequences of Jacob deceiving Laban and fleeing secretly.
Laban confronts Jacob and asks why he fled secretly and 'stole his heart' – a direct follow-up that uses the same expression as verse 20.
Absalom 'stole the hearts' of Israel's men (vayyegnov... et-lev). The same Hebrew idiom (ganav lev) as in Genesis 31:20, used regarding deception.
The Lord commanded Jacob to return to his homeland, which is the divine background for Jacob's decision to leave Laban.
Laban and Jacob make a covenant at Galeed as a result of Jacob's secret flight, showing reconciliation after the deception.
